subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the independent variable in an experiment?
options: The variable that is deliberately changed by the investigator
The variable that is measured as the outcome
A variable that is kept constant throughout
A variable that changes randomly and cannot be controlled
questions.explain: The independent variable is the one the investigator alters to see its effect on the dependent variable.

questions.q: What is the dependent variable?
options: The variable that is measured or observed as the result
The variable that is changed by the investigator
A variable kept the same to make the test fair
The equipment used to take readings
questions.explain: The dependent variable is the outcome that is measured and depends on the independent variable.

questions.q: A measurement is described as accurate when it is:
options: Consistent between repeats but not necessarily correct
questions.explain: Accuracy describes how close a measurement is to the true (accepted) value.

questions.q: A set of measurements is described as precise when the values are:
questions.explain: Precision refers to how closely repeated measurements agree with each other, regardless of the true value.

questions.q: Which piece of apparatus is most suitable for accurately measuring a fixed volume of liquid?
questions.explain: A measuring cylinder gives an accurate volume reading, whereas a beaker's markings are only approximate.

questions.q: Which reagent is used to test a food sample for starch, and what colour change shows a positive result?
questions.explain: Iodine solution turns from orange-brown to blue-black in the presence of starch.

questions.q: Which test is used to detect reducing sugars in a food sample?
options: Benedict's test, heating with the sample
questions.explain: Benedict's solution is heated with the sample and turns from blue to green/orange/brick-red if reducing sugar is present.

questions.q: How is the range of a set of results calculated?
options: The sum of the values divided by the number of values
The middle value when data are ordered
questions.explain: The range is the difference between the largest and smallest values in a data set.

questions.q: The resolution of a measuring instrument is best described as:
options: The smallest change in a quantity it can detect
How close its readings are to the true value
The largest quantity it can measure
How quickly it gives a reading
questions.explain: Resolution is the smallest change in the measured quantity that produces a detectable change in the reading.

questions.q: Results are said to be reproducible when:
options: Similar results are obtained by a different person or using different equipment
The same person gets similar results by repeating the method
The results are recorded to the same number of decimal places
questions.explain: Reproducibility means similar results are achieved when the investigation is repeated by others or with different apparatus.

questions.q: In a risk assessment, what is the difference between a hazard and a risk?
options: A hazard is something that could cause harm; a risk is the chance that harm actually occurs
A hazard is the chance of harm; a risk is the object causing harm
They mean exactly the same thing
A hazard applies only to chemicals; a risk applies only to equipment
questions.explain: A hazard is anything with the potential to cause harm, while risk is the likelihood of that harm happening.

questions.q: Why would an investigator use a quadrat when sampling plants in a field?
options: To estimate the number or distribution of organisms in a known area
To measure the mass of the plants
To measure the temperature of the soil
questions.explain: A quadrat marks out a known area so the abundance or distribution of organisms can be sampled and estimated.

questions.q: A student obtains the readings 12, 13, 12, 45 and 13 seconds. How should the value of 45 be treated?
options: It is anomalous and should be excluded when calculating the mean
It should be included so the mean is fair
It should replace the lowest value
It shows the experiment is precise
questions.explain: An anomalous result lies well outside the pattern of other data and should be ignored when calculating the mean.

questions.q: Which type of graph is most appropriate for displaying data where both variables are continuous?
questions.explain: A line graph is used when both the independent and dependent variables are continuous numerical data.

questions.q: Why does an investigator repeat readings and calculate a mean?
options: To reduce the effect of random errors and improve reliability
To increase the resolution of the instrument
To make the experiment take longer
questions.explain: Repeating readings and averaging reduces the influence of random errors, giving a more reliable result.

questions.q: How is the total magnification of a light microscope calculated?
options: Eyepiece lens magnification multiplied by objective lens magnification
Eyepiece lens magnification added to objective lens magnification
Objective lens magnification divided by eyepiece lens magnification
Image size divided by objective lens magnification
questions.explain: Total magnification is found by multiplying the eyepiece magnification by the objective lens magnification.

questions.q: A student records reaction times of 24, 26 and 25 seconds. What is the mean?
questions.explain: The mean is (24 + 26 + 25) / 3 = 75 / 3 = 25 seconds.

questions.q: A microscope has an eyepiece lens of x10 and an objective lens of x40. What is the total magnification?
questions.explain: Total magnification = 10 x 40 = x400.

questions.q: The image of a cell measures 40 mm across and the magnification is x200. What is the actual size of the cell?
questions.explain: Actual size = image size / magnification = 40 / 200 = 0.2 mm.

questions.q: An investigation measures how light intensity affects the rate of photosynthesis in pondweed. Which of these should be kept as a control variable?
options: The distance of the lamp from the pondweed
questions.explain: Temperature must be kept constant so that only light intensity (the independent variable) affects the measured rate.
